text:
sam: Heads-up — I pushed a change to package.json exports to standardize on conditional exports (import/require) and it looks like a couple customer edge runtimes + our Next edge sample app are failing with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED :facepalm:

maria: ugh sorry — which export map did you add? can you paste snippet?

sam: Sure, current exports I pushed:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

sam: Repro is: Next edge (middleware/edge runtime) imports the SDK like `import SDK from 'redwood-inference'` and the runtime resolver tries to use the CJS path and fails to resolve default, throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED for some bundlers. Also TypeScript users see typings missing for the mjs path.

jon: I think some edge runtimes (V8 isolates/deno/next edge) prefer the `import` condition but bundlers can pick `require` when they expect cjs. If package has both, but dist files don't include proper export subpaths, the resolver can get confused.

alex: Another wrinkle — our types field currently points to "./dist/index.d.ts" but when consumers use `exports` without an explicit `types` condition TS can't always infer. Some consumers reported "Could not find a declaration file for module 'redwood-inference'" in the sample app.

megan: Any quick mitigations while we investigate? revert the export map? publish a patch?

sam: Quick repro steps I added to the failing sample app repo: create Next 13 edge middleware, import SDK, run `next dev` -> immediate crash in edge with stack: `Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: No "exports" main defined for 'redwood-inference'`

maria: Proposed fix options:
1) Expand exports with explicit edge/browser conditions and a `default` fallback:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "edge": "./dist/edge.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
    "default": "./dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
2) Add `types` conditional export mapping (some bundlers support it) and keep `types` top-level: "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
3) Add `module`/`main` fields back for older tools: "module": "./dist/index.mjs", "main": "./dist/index.cjs"

jon: I prefer option 1 + module/main for max compatibility. Also add a tiny index at top-level that re-exports proper default to avoid CJS default interop surprises: `dist/interop.cjs` with `module.exports = require('./index.cjs').default || require('./index.cjs')` and point require to that.

alex: For types, do this too in export map: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  }
}
```
Not all TS versions honor that, but it helps with bundlers that do.

megan: I'll open a small patch PR that implements 1+3 and adds a note in changelog and upgrade guide explaining the export map changes and how to consume from edge runtimes. linking here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/142 (ci-bot will run tests)

ci-bot: CI started for PR #142 — running matrix (node 16/18, ts 4.9/5.1) :gear:

sam: Thanks. Long-term we should add a tiny compatibility test matrix in our e2e sample apps: Next edge + Vercel edge + Deno import and a TS consumer. That would have caught this before shipping.

maria: Agreed. Also add a lint rule to fail CI if export map is changed without bumping semver and adding compat notes.

jon: FYI, the downstream plugin ecosystem (esbuild/rollup/webpack loaders) all behave slightly differently; call it the export-map cold war. :sweat_smile:

alex: Patch LGTM in initial review — will merge after green CI.

megan: I'll leave the sample app pinned to the patched release and ping any early adopters who hit the issue.

sam: Good catch everyone — thanks for quick turnaround. We'll follow up with a short postmortem in #devex after merge with what went wrong and checklist for future export map changes.
